method: Read existing aggregate/server log/recording source; ffprobe each existing expected MP4, concurrency=2. No inference, UI control, recording restart, production changes, or media repair.
ffprobe_version: ffprobe version 9.0.1 Copyright (c) 2007-2026 the FFmpeg developers

code_findings.finding: defaultSpawn pipes stdout/stderr but does not drain or retain either stream. Its returned interface exposes only exited and kill.
record.started is logged immediately after spawn, without waiting for first frame, an output file, or successful process initialization.
awaitExit only treats timeout as failure. Numeric child exit codes, including nonzero, are not checked or recorded.
stopQuietly logs record.stopped and returns the expected path once stop resolves; file existence, size, MP4 structure and video duration are not checked.

conclusion.observed: All missing paths are reported separately below; recording event success is not evidence that a playable video file exists.
conclusion.mechanism_supported_by_code: An early scrcpy process failure/nonzero exit can still produce record.started followed by record.stopped and a non-null video path under the current implementation.
conclusion.specific_cause_of_missing_six: Unknown: these sessions did not preserve scrcpy exit codes or stdout/stderr. The saved data cannot distinguish process initialization/encoder failure from another cause or later file removal.
conclusion.impact: Six case videos are unavailable; existing screenshots and structured action/UI logs remain independent evidence. Model case verdicts were not changed by this recording audit.
conclusion.limits: ffprobe validates container metadata, a video stream, nonzero dimensions and positive duration. It does not decode every frame, visually review footage, or prove complete temporal coverage of the case.
